source: original; stimulus is a public-domain photograph viewed before writing (see figures)

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Elvis Presley, 1956 publicity portrait. Public domain (published in the United States in 1956 without a copyright notice), via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph is a 1956 publicity portrait of Elvis Presley, a white singer from Memphis, Tennessee. Presley, with his slicked-back hair, became the most famous performer of the new rock 'n' roll music.

stem: Presley's fame best shows which feature of 1950s youth culture?

options.text: Teenagers rejected all music their parents had enjoyed
options.misconception: Background from the books: teenagers kept listening to many older styles, so they did not reject all of them.

options.text: Television networks banned rock 'n' roll from the air entirely
options.misconception: Background from the books: Presley performed on television, so the networks did not ban rock.

options.text: A white star carried Black-rooted music to white teens
Rock 'n' roll faded away before the decade ended
options.misconception: Background from the books: rock grew tamer and more commercial, but it did not fade away.

rationales.A: Background from the books: teenagers kept listening to many older styles, so they did not reject all of them.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Presley performed on television, so the networks did not ban rock.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Presley, a white singer, followed Black performers such as Chuck Berry and brought their music to white teenagers.
rationales.D: Background from the books: rock grew tamer and more commercial, but it did not fade away.
rationales.general:
1. Presley was white, and the photograph shows a star marketed to a mass audience.
2. Background from the books: the music he sang grew from Black rhythm and blues, gospel, and the blues.
3. Background from the books: a white star singing Black-rooted music let white teenagers enjoy it while the color line still stood.
Remember: When a star crosses a social line, ask whose work the star carries across it.
